clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 pickup, often a snorkel
text: Kenya is mostly covered in Generation 4 **pickup truck coverage**. Most trucks are blurred out, but sometimes you can see parts of the car, which can be many different colors, or a **snorkel**.
NOTE: It is the only country other than Mongolia with a snorkel in Generation 4.
clues.summary: Mostly a Gen 4 pickup truck. It is usually blurred, but you may see parts of it in many colours, or a raised antenna pipe (snorkel). Only Mongolia also has a snorkel in Gen 4.

clues.title: Road lines: solid white outer, yellow inner
text: Outer lines in Kenya will always be solid white, while inner lines will be yellow and either solid or dashed.
clues.summary: Outer lines are always solid white, while inner lines are yellow, either solid or dashed.

clues.title: Pole: concrete or wood, L-shaped crossbar
text: Kenyan poles are either made of concrete or wood, and have an** L shaped crossbar**.
NOTE: A [similar pole](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tZNFYkUB6yvXdjgn6) can be found in Ghana
clues.summary: Concrete or wooden poles with an L-shaped crossbar. Ghana has a similar pole.

clues.title: Google car: grey SUV following behind
text: On a lot of the coverage you will see a grey Toyota SUV following the Street View car.
clues.summary: In a lot of the coverage a grey Toyota SUV follows the Street View car.

clues.title: Plate: long white front, square yellow rear
text: Kenya uses **long white** front licence plates. The rear counterpart is **square** and **yellow**.

images.caption: Kenyan plates: long white front and square yellow rear

clues.summary: Front plates are long and white, while rear plates are square and yellow.

clues.title: Phone network: one brand in every city
text: This mobile network brand named **Safaricom **is unique to Kenya, and almost every city has one location.
clues.summary: A mobile network brand, Safaricom, is unique to this country, and almost every city has a shop for it.

clues.title: Sign: green direction sign, white border
text: Directional signs are **green **with a white border and text. They often display road numbers in white or [yellow](https://goo.gl/maps/DqEYtasj9mwbfE3G7).
clues.summary: Green direction signs with a white border and text. Road numbers show in white or yellow.

clues.title: Sign: red and white road signs
text: While infrequent, road signs in Kenya will mostly be **red and white**.
clues.summary: Road signs are not frequent, but the ones you see are mostly red and white.

clues.title: Vans: repurposed vans with wrapped designs
text: These **repurposed vans** can be found all over Kenya.
NOTE: While these vans can also be found in Uganda, the [design](https://goo.gl/maps/zn7PBhoaiJuyv6Ju7) of the vehicle wrap is clearly different.

images.caption: A wrapped-design repurposed van on a highway; the circle shows a yellow dashed road line

clues.summary: Repurposed vans with colourful wraps are everywhere. Uganda has them too, but the wrap design is clearly different.

differs.how: The wrap design on the vans is clearly different

clues.title: Plants: eucalyptus with long leaves
text: Many species of **eucalyptus **are commonly found in Kenya. They can be identified by their long, often clumped leaves, and smooth bark.
NOTE: Eucalyptus trees can be found in other countries. Use this information to help reinforce your country guess.

images.caption: Eucalyptus trees, with circled close-ups of the long leaves and the smooth bark

clues.summary: Many kinds of eucalyptus, with long, often clumped leaves and smooth bark. They grow in other countries too, so use this only to back up a guess.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 roof rack and snorkel
text: Generation 3 coverage in Kenya often features a **visible roof rack ** and a **snorkel**. Some Generation 3 coverage has [no visible car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UGBAo7hH2mhLsUv46).

images.caption: Four Gen 3 shots showing the roof rack and snorkel, with the red label Gen 3

clues.summary: Gen 3 coverage often shows a roof rack and a raised antenna pipe (snorkel). Some Gen 3 coverage shows no car at all.

clues.title: Pole: skull and danger warning marking
text: You will often see pole markings with a **skull** and a **danger message** on it.
clues.summary: Poles often carry a marking with a skull and a danger message.

clues.title: Sign: county name written on signs and posters
text: Upon closer inspection of signs, billboards and posters, you will notice that the **county name** is often written. Therefore, knowledge of Kenyan counties can be extremely useful in region guessing.
_You can practise Kenyan counties using the quiz in the resource section._

images.caption: Sign naming Makueni County, with a red box around the county name

clues.summary: Signs, billboards and posters often show the county name, which helps a lot with narrowing down the region.

clues.title: Coverage: mainly main roads outside southwest
text: Most of the coverage in Kenya outside of the southwest is limited to **main roads**.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Outside the southwest, coverage is mostly just main roads.

clues.title: Sign: PO BOX with post code number
text: Post codes in Kenya can be identified by [signs in the format PO BOX XXX-YYYZZ](https://maps.app.goo.gl/zkoZ8sYzmTGiRivA6), where the number YYY (usually 3 digits but sometimes 0) corresponds to a post code. This is the number which can be used to narrow down your guess. Often, the name of the city is listed after the PO BOX.
NOTE: You can sometimes see [PO BOX without the second number](https://maps.app.goo.gl/sNta3QHeJpwVVgoDA) after the hyphen which is not helpful.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it. Here is a _[quiz](https://www.super-duper.fr/quiz2024/areacodes.php?country=POST_KE&language=en&tile=gmaps&border=thin&difficulty=false&timer=false&gmaplng=en)_ to help practice Kenyan post codes_
clues.summary: Signs read like PO BOX XXX-YYYZZ. The number YYY is a post code that narrows down the area, and often the city name follows. A PO BOX with no second number is not helpful.

clues.title: Landscape: flat east and north
text: The natural formation of land has great diversity between regions. The east and large portions of the north are extremely flat. In contrast, the further southwest you travel, the higher the elevation becomes on average.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: The east and large parts of the north are extremely flat. The further southwest you go, the higher the land gets.

clues.title: Climate: humid, semi-arid, arid, very arid
text: Kenya has distinct regional climates. Some of these include:
- [Humid](https://goo.gl/maps/ikoiFyXWzkoo89Yd6)
- [Semi-Arid](https://goo.gl/maps/8pKMM9UmiABeQ5JWA)
- [Arid ](https://goo.gl/maps/WM987ahC4aCCZtLB9)
- [Very-Arid](https://goo.gl/maps/cysAiN7mGE66ZSJ97)
As regions vary, this means that there will be many transitional climates. Use this as a guide to quickly determine the general area to assist with region guessing.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Different regions have distinct climates: humid, semi-arid, arid and very arid, with transitional climates between. Use the dryness to guess the general area.

clues.title: Landscape: farms, grassy hills, tall eucalyptus
text: The far west areas of the country that are northwest and southwest of Kisumu are the most agricultural parts of the country. You will often see **farms**, grassy hills, and tall **eucalyptus **trees in this region of the country.
clues.summary: In the far west, the most agricultural area: farms, grassy hills and tall eucalyptus trees.

clues.title: Landscape: semi-arid, mountainous
text: The area around Kitui is **semi-arid**, usually mountainous, and has light orange, sandy dirt.
clues.summary: Semi-arid, usually mountainous land with light orange, sandy dirt.

clues.title: Landscape: tan soil, sparse low trees
text: The northwest part of the country has very limited coverage, most of which is on the A1 or in Sibiloi National Park. It has faintly **tan soil **and sparse** low trees**. A lot of the coverage in this area is very flat, but you can also see hills or mountains.
NOTE: Most of this coverage has a [dirty exposed car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/AVaanekywEYdiAqm6).
clues.summary: In the northwest, with very limited coverage: faintly tan soil and sparse low trees, mostly flat but sometimes with hills. The car is usually dirty and exposed.

clues.title: Plants: coconut palms
text: Coastal Kenya can be identified by the presence of **coconut palms**, with rare areas in Taita-Taveta County also containing them.
clues.summary: Coconut palms point to the coast, and rarely to one inland county.

clues.title: Plants: lots of white flowers
text: **White flowers**, especially when they are in large numbers, are commonly found east of Chyulu Hills National Park, as well as in Tsavo National Park and near the A109 south of Nairobi.
clues.summary: Large numbers of white flowers are common in parts of the south, near a national park and south of the capital.

clues.title: Fences: endless stick fences
text: Stick fences which **seem to go on forever** are common in the area around Narok.
clues.summary: Stick fences that seem to go on forever are common in one area of the southwest.

clues.title: Houses: red brick
text: **Red brick architecture** is common in the western part of the country and a large area east of Nairobi.
clues.summary: Red brick buildings are common in the west and in a large area east of the capital.

clues.title: Houses: mud and sticks
text: Houses that are made of **mud and sticks** are commonly seen around the western part of the country and the coast.
clues.summary: Houses made of mud and sticks are common in the west and on the coast.

clues.title: Walls: light bricks with thick mortar
text: These **light color bricks** with **excessive amounts of mortar** are found along the coast. [Walls](https://maps.app.goo.gl/k9LPg72T65jHNfLi8) made of these bricks are commonly seen in this area.
clues.summary: Light-coloured bricks with a lot of mortar between them, in walls along the coast.

clues.title: Google car: unusual cars near national parks
text: Kenya has many **unique **Google cars in and around its National Parks and Reserves. These are still identifiable by the snorkel which is present in almost all of them.
Many of the National Park and Reserve cars must be used in conjunction with landscape, as they can be found in multiple areas.
_You can learn more about these National Parks and Reserves in the spotlight section._
clues.summary: Many unusual cars around national parks and reserves, almost all with a snorkel (a raised antenna pipe). You need the landscape too, as many cars appear in several places.

clues.title: Road: unpaved, bright reddish-orange dirt
text: The B9 in the Northeast is entirely unpaved and has bright **reddish orange dirt **with many trees surrounding the road. Most of it is very flat, but the coverage at the western end of the road can have hills and mountains. The soil also transitions into a more sandy colour.
clues.summary: An entirely unpaved road with bright reddish-orange dirt and many trees. Mostly flat, with hills at the western end, where the soil turns sandier.

clues.title: Landscape: plants by the road, big mountains
text: The A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit has many plants alongside the road and you will often see **large mountains **in the distance. The stretch going through Namunyak Wildlife Conservation Trust will have a very large mountain range to the west.
clues.summary: A road with many plants beside it and large mountains in the distance. One stretch has a very large mountain range to the west.

clues.title: Landscape: much flatter, few plants
text: North of Marsabit will be **much flatter**, with some mountains in the distance. The stretch just north or Marsabit will have mountains visible to the south, while further north, a different range can be seen. It will also have much less vegetation.
clues.summary: North of a mountain town the land is much flatter with less vegetation. Mountains are visible in the distance, to the south at first and a different range further north.

clues.title: Landscape: light soil, many green trees
text: The A3 north of Garissa is very unique, with **light coloured **soil and many green trees on either side of the road.
clues.summary: A road with light-coloured soil and many green trees on both sides.

clues.title: Landscape: flat road, sugar cane
text: The western part of the C34 is a flat, **east to west** road. There are two long, straight sections with an abundance of **sugar cane**. Furthermore, you will see a large **mountain range** **north** along the entire mentioned stretches of road.
clues.summary: A flat east-west road with two long straight sections of sugar cane, and a large mountain range to the north throughout.

clues.title: City: skyscrapers, dense
text: Nairobi is the largest city in the country, and capital of Kenya. It is the only city to have a considerable amount of **skyscrapers**,** **and is highly developed. It is densely populated, and is surrounded by small, poor settlements.
clues.summary: The capital is the only city with many skyscrapers. It is very developed and dense, surrounded by small, poor settlements.

clues.title: View: huge mountain to the south
text: In a lot of the coverage north of **Mt Kilimanjaro**, the mountain is visible to the south, usually obscured by clouds. In the city of [Oloitoktok](https://goo.gl/maps/aRSZy6jApL8BNXkm7), the mountain will often be visible directly to the south.
NOTE: The map shows the location of Mt Kilimanjaro, but it can be seen from very far away.
clues.summary: In lots of coverage in the south, a huge mountain sits to the south, usually hidden by cloud. In one town it is often directly south.

clues.title: Landscape: protruding hill to the east
text: Homa Bay has this **protruding hill** to the east that is often visible.
clues.summary: A lakeside town with a protruding hill to the east that is often visible.

clues.title: Road: blinding white dirt
text: The city of Wajir often has blinding white dirt roads, combined with extremely red soil on the roadside.
clues.summary: Blinding white dirt roads combined with extremely red soil beside the road.

clues.title: Landscape: flat or hilly, no mountains
text: Mara Triangle has no considerable mountains and most of it is either **flat or hilly**. It has a white car that can be found in other Kenyan National Parks. [Generation 4 coverage](https://maps.app.goo.gl/bKJA3RRXboNWPdgD8) exists there as well.
clues.summary: A reserve with no big mountains, mostly flat or hilly. It has a white car that also appears in other national parks, and Gen 4 coverage exists there too.

clues.title: Google car: grey, small snorkel, flat tan grass
text: Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with **tan grass, few trees**, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.
clues.summary: A grey car with a small snorkel in a very flat area with tan grass, few trees and dried lake beds. The base of a huge mountain is always visible to the south, mostly in cloud.

clues.title: Google car: grey and brown, big snorkel
text: Aberdare National Park** **has a **grey and brown** car that features a large snorkel. Almost all of the coverage is outside of the National Park, with only two roads within the park covered. The main road through the park has [these](https://goo.gl/maps/g4D2K3mtsHqrAwKr7) rubber bands on the roof rack, which can only be found in one other National Park in Kenya.
clues.summary: A grey and brown car with a large snorkel. Almost all coverage is outside the park; the main road inside has rubber bands on the roof rack, found in only one other park.

clues.title: Google car: grey-brown car with rubber bands
text: Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, you can find the Aberdare car as well, but it will always have **rubber bands**, unlike in Aberdare where it will only have them on the main roads through the park. It can be differentiated from Aberdare by its redder dirt, and **greener **landscape.

images.caption: Google car seen from above; the circled zoom shows rubber bands tied on the car, arrow pointing to them.

clues.summary: The same car as the grey-and-brown park car, but always with rubber bands. Redder dirt and a greener landscape tell it apart from the park.

clues.title: Google car: grey-brown car in sandy, dry land
text: The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses the same car as the Aberdare National Park, but with a vastly different landscape. It is very **sandy, dry**, and has little vegetation.
You may also find yourself in [Generation 3 coverage without car meta](https://goo.gl/maps/SVmfuG3XAkPt2ipv7).
clues.summary: The same car as the grey-and-brown park car but in very sandy, dry land with little vegetation. You may also meet Gen 3 coverage without any car.

clues.title: Roadside: many succulents
text: This stretch of the B8 just north of Kibaoni has many **succulents **on the side of the road.
clues.summary: A stretch of road with many succulents along the side.

clues.title: Google car: two bird droppings
text: Only on a very tiny bit of coverage on the C104 in southern Kenya, embedded in Tsavo National Park, the Google car is adorned with two recognizable splats of bird poop. Cheers.

images.caption: Two orange circles mark bird droppings on the dusty grey car hood

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On one tiny bit of coverage inside a national park, the car has two clear splats of bird poop.

clues.title: Google car: white tape on roof
text: You can see pieces of white tape on the roof of the Google car in a lot of the coverage north and south of Nairobi.

images.caption: Circle and arrow at top left point to a detail on the Google car roof

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Pieces of white tape are visible on the car's roof in a lot of the coverage around the capital.

clues.title: Landscape: white sand, palms, coastal feel
text: Mombasa and the other coastal towns are easily identified from the white sandy soil, palm trees and coastal feel.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Coastal towns are easy to spot by white sandy soil, palm trees and a seaside feel.

clues.title: Google car: cord on left, light orange dirt
text: The A109 between Mombasa and Nairobi has light orange dirt and many hills around the road and in the distance.
Most of the coverage between Mombasa and Emali also has a unique car, which has a cord on the left.

images.caption: Circled zoom with arrow shows the cord on the left side of the Google car, on light orange dirt.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A road with light orange dirt and many hills nearby and in the distance. Most of this coverage has a car with a cord on the left.

clues.title: Google car: covered in specks of dirt
text: This car that is covered in specks of dirt is unique to these stretches of the A3, B9, and the Habaswein-Dadaab Road connecting the two.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A car covered in specks of dirt, unique to a few roads in the north and east.

clues.title: Pole: wooden with metal top bar and support
text: Kenya use wooden poles with a metallic topbar and support.
NOTE: Panama use mostly concrete poles with wooden support. Good to know for 50/50

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Wooden poles with a metal top bar and support. Panama mostly has concrete poles with a wooden support, handy for a 50/50.

differs.how: Panamanian poles are mostly concrete with wooden support
